title: POC Weekly - Redwood Private VPC Pilot Sync

Priya to provide updated VPN config and Alex to share patch for the helm chart. Customer asked for SOC2 artifact pointer and KMS integration notes.

Failed canary deployment and rollback reasons
Benchmark results post quantization and batching tweaks
Next steps: network diagram + security deep-dive

Alex to share helm/chart patch & canary logs (by 2026-08-28)

transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-08-26
- Time: 15:00 PDT
- Duration: ~46 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (BrightPath Platform Eng), Maya Rivera (BrightPath Security), Tom Hsu (SRE), Leah Park (Product), Chris Gonzales (CTO)

Summary/Notes (auto):
Priya walked through last week's patch, we validated telemetry and KV cache behavior, saw one canary fail due to routing mismatch (BGP vs static route), customer to run a second benchmark post-helm patch. Security asks for SOC2 artifact pointers and KMS integration notes. Next steps captured in action items.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we got about 45 minutes, I think, uh goal for today is quick status on the network fixes and the canary, and then the benchmark numbers that Jordan ran overnight.
[00:14] Jordan Lee: Thanks Alex, yeah, quick note up front, the overnight runs used the trunk model with 4-bit quant and the Redwood batching suggestions, numbers look promising but latency spiked at tail percentiles.
[00:28] Priya Patel: okay, yeah so the quant+batching config we pushed reduced avg token cost by ~22% but as you saw the p99 went up a bit on the long prompts. We think that's due to some routing fallbacks - requests jumping between AZs due to the transit gateway rules.
[00:44] Tom Hsu: yep we saw that in our traces. At ~02:30 UTC you can see requests hit a different subnet and then the KV cache miss rate increased, so cold cache plus cross-AZ latency.
[00:59] Maya Rivera: just to clarify, is that coming from the VPC peering changes or the NAT gateway? I thought we had peering in place.
[01:12] Priya Patel: good question, so currently the peering is up but there's a route table overlap - there's a more specific static route in one AZ that causes a route preference, the transit GW will prefer that and cause some traffic to exit and reenter. It's subtle.
[01:27] Leah Park: sorry quick dumb question, is that the same thing as VPC-to-VPC peering versus a transit gateway? I wanna make sure I understand the pattern.
[01:37] Alex Kim: yeah, Leah, good callout. Peerings are direct and more static; transit gateway is central routing. We recommended transit for scale but you need to make sure route priorities and BGP if used are consistent.
[01:49] Jordan Lee: the canary - so we ran a small canary yesterday and it failed partially. The rollout showed 2 instances flagged as unhealthy after the model warmup step, then the rollback kicked in. Logs show TLS handshake retries and a couple of 502s from the proxy.
[02:04] Priya Patel: right, I dug in on the canary. The failure chain started with the SNI being set to an internal host that didn't match the certs in the private cluster - some of the helper containers were referencing the old service name due to a stale env var in the helm template.
[02:20] Alex Kim: ugh, that env var swap is my fault, we missed that in the last merge. Priya, can you patch the chart to make the service name templated?
[02:28] Priya Patel: yep i'll push a patch after this call and Alex will share the canary logs.
[02:35] Chris Gonzales: from a security/compliance perspective, we need the SOC2 docs and also specifics on how KMS is used. Are the keys customer-managed or Redwood-managed in this private deployment?
[02:49] Priya Patel: in Private we support both patterns. For this pilot we recommended customer-managed keys via your KMS, the integration is via IAM role and the Redwood runtime fetches a data encryption key per-instance. We'll send the integration notes.
[03:05] Maya Rivera: and the audit logs - where do they land? We need them in our SIEM for 90 days minimum.
[03:12] Alex Kim: audit logs can be forwarded to your logging endpoint or delivered via S3 and you can configure retention. We'll include a sample lambda/forwarder for Splunk and for Sumo Logic.
[03:24] Tom Hsu: back to networking - Jordan and I tried toggling the NAT to force all egress through the same AZ but that caused increased egress costs and didn't fully fix the p99. We think fixing the routing table precedence is the right approach.
[03:38] Jordan Lee: yep and once we fix that, we expect the KV cache hit rate to go back up which should reduce p99.
[03:44] Priya Patel: also a small note on batching: we adjusted the batching window to 25ms for low-latency paths, that helped avg but can make tail worse for bursty traffic. We're recommending dynamic windowing for production.
[03:58] Leah Park: dynamic windowing meaning - like based on token backlog or CPU utilization?
[04:06] Priya Patel: yeah token backlog is primary signal, secondarily GPU utilization and queue depth. We'll include config suggestions in the notes.
[04:15] Chris Gonzales: what's the timeline to get the canary stable? We need to hit the mid-Sept milestone for pilot signoff.
[04:22] Alex Kim: we can have the helm patch and re-run the canary this week. If networking change is validated by Jordan by Monday we'll re-run a full canary Tuesday and then a bigger smoke test Wed. So looks feasible for mid-Sept.
[04:36] Jordan Lee: one more datapoint on benchmarks: throughput was good, CPU/GPU ratio improved with the quantization but we saw 4xx spikes when front proxy retried requests - those correlate to the cert/SNI mismatch Priya mentioned.
[04:50] Priya Patel: ok noted, Alex will share the specific proxy logs. Also on the model side, we tried a different kernel selection for the attention op and that shaved off ~12ms avg, unclear effect on long sequences yet.
[05:06] Tom Hsu: can you explain kernel selection quickly? I remember Priya mentioned something about compilation choices.
[05:13] Priya Patel: sure, the runtime picks optimized kernels based on seq-len distribution and the hardware, sometimes the default path isn't best for longer sequences. We can force an alternate kernel at the node level to test. It's safe for canary.
[05:25] Maya Rivera: re: security deep-dive, I'd like a separate call with your security lead to go over key rotation, HSM options, and where logs live. Also need to see evidence for SOC2 controls around change management.
[05:39] Alex Kim: absolutely, we can schedule that. I'll loop in our security PM and send a proposed slot.
[05:46] Jordan Lee: quick question - what's the recommended approach for peering vs transit given our multi-account setup? We have 6 accounts and traffic patterns are cross-account.
[05:57] Priya Patel: transit gateway is usually recommended at that scale, but you have to be careful with route propagation and VRF-like isolation. For strict isolation you can do multiple TGWs or attach route tables per attachment. We'll include examples.
[06:11] Leah Park: small UI note: in the console the per-route latency graphs aren't aligning with our ingested traces sometimes, might be due to mismatch in sampling windows.
[06:22] Alex Kim: good catch, that's likely sampling. We'll double-check the tracing hook config we asked you to set last week.
[06:30] Chris Gonzales: ok wrapping up - what are the concrete deliverables before the next sync?
[06:36] Alex Kim: recap: Priya will send VPN/routing guide, Alex will upload canary logs and helm patch, Jordan will validate routing, Maya will list SOC2/KMS questions, customer to run second benchmark after patch. We'll aim to re-run canary Tuesday.
[06:52] Maya Rivera: thanks all, and please include the KMS key policy example and a sample IAM role.
[06:59] Priya Patel: will do, I'll also add the dynamic batching config options.
[07:05] Alex Kim: cool, thanks everyone, we'll follow up via the shared drive and ping for the security deep-dive times.
